algorithm.Title: Eye - Allergy - Female (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Female
Definition: Qatar-localized UAT-only adult and pediatric pathway for suspected allergic eye symptoms, screening for sight-threatening disease, trauma, chemical exposure, infection, contact-lens risk and neonatal illness; not approved for production.
FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 for major trauma, collapse or severe systemic deterioration; otherwise proceed immediately to the locally approved emergency eye destination. Do not drive with impaired vision, rub the eye, remove an embedded object or apply drops after chemical exposure unless directed. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Was the eye exposed to a chemical, acid, cleaning product, or unknown liquid?
questions.Information: Begin immediate continuous irrigation and obtain emergency in-person assessment; the source-only chemical-eye family is not generated.

questions.Question: Is there sudden or reduced vision, severe eye pain, chemical exposure, penetrating/embedded object, major injury, abnormal pupil, or eye symptoms with severe headache, vomiting, confusion or rapid deterioration?
questions.Information: NHS.UK conjunctivitis guidance lists these as signs of a more serious eye problem needing urgent clinical review or emergency assessment.

questions.Question: Is this a baby with red, sticky eyes, does the caller wear contact lenses with eyelid spots, or have symptoms not cleared within 7 days?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends a primary-care review for these situations.

questions.Question: After emergency features are excluded, are itchy or watery eyes still presumed to be allergy without an in-person examination?
questions.Information: Remote assessment cannot safely confirm allergy or exclude infection, corneal disease, foreign body or contact-lens complications in this UAT pathway.

advice.Title: Emergency eye precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 for major trauma, collapse or severe systemic deterioration; otherwise proceed immediately to the locally approved emergency eye destination. Do not drive with impaired vision, rub the eye, remove an embedded object or apply drops after chemical exposure unless directed. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: vision worsens; pain, vomiting or confusion increases.

advice.Title: Priority eye assessment
Content: Arrange prompt in-person assessment through the Qatar pathway approved for UAT. Neonates, contact-lens wearers and immunocompromised patients need age/risk-specific review. Stop wearing contact lenses until clinically cleared.
Call Back If: symptoms worsen; pain, light sensitivity or vision change develops.

advice.Title: In-person assessment of presumed eye allergy
Content: Avoid rubbing the eyes and stop contact-lens wear. Arrange in-person assessment before selecting drops or antihistamines; age, pregnancy, allergy, glaucoma and interactions must be checked.
Call Back If: pain, light sensitivity or vision change; swelling, fever or systemic allergy develops.
